pull.title: util: Make files opened with fdbridge::fopen noninheritable
pull.body:
Fixes #36668

Use the 'e' mode on POSIX to set close-on-exec and the 'N' mode on windows to prevent file handle inheritance by child processes.

This PR is still in WIP... until I add some test cases and verify that it works on Windows and Mac. I've only tested it on Linux (OpenSUSE Tumbleweed)

I tested `fsbridge::fopen` at `ca864d2fc1` with a standalone MSVC test using `fs.cpp`. The file was opened in append mode (`"a"`), and handle inheritance was enabled in `CreateProcessW`. After the parent closed the file, `DeleteFileW` failed with `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` on the pre-PR code. With this change, deletion succeeded while the child was still alive.

The compilation errors in `fs_tests.cpp` prevent `test_bitcoin` from building on Windows.

comments.body: Is "e" available on all non-Windows systems?
Unfortunately, the consecutive `fopen` and `fcntl(..., FD_CLOEXEC)` calls are not atomic, which is a race in a multithreaded process.
Could we keep the original `e` approach on Linux and handle macOS separately with `open` using `O_CLOEXEC`, followed by `fdopen`?
Yes, you are right, I will try to find a solution on how I can make it safe under multi threaded processes.

I changed implementation into three cases 

1. linux
3. windows
4. posix
